h: Shabbos Reveals the Torah Hidden Within Creation

p: "And if his offering is a sacrifice of shelamim."
(בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ, חֵלֶק ג יא, ב)
(In the holy Zohar, this parsha, III 11b):
"Ten, ten": what does this come to teach?
Rather, ten for the act of Creation
and ten for the giving of the Torah, etc.;
they are weighed together on a single scale.
"Remember the Shabbos day to sanctify it,"
when is the holy land made to flourish
to bring forth growth and blessings to the world.
corresponds to the attribute of Chessed;
corresponds to the attribute of Chessed,
which is the spreading forth of His kindness, may He be blessed,
to bestow sustenance on His creatures,
which is the sustaining of man's life
כִּי אֱלֹקִים עָשָׂה אֶת הָאָדָם יָשָׁר
meaning that he was to be nourished in Gan Eden
from the fruit of the trees of the garden;
and this is the root of his life in holiness,
"And they beheld God, and they ate";
and Chazal, of blessed memory, said
That is the root of the eating and drinking
and drink of the wine I have mixed";
and like the eating of the man,
and as is written in the holy Zohar
their sustenance comes from a higher place,
'Wisdom gives life to those who possess it.'"
And this is the root of the attribute of Chessed,
וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא זָן אוֹתָם בְּחַסְדּוֹ
when HaKadosh Baruch Hu sustained them in His kindness;
and for this reason it is called the Great Hallel,
sits in the heights of the world
and apportions food to all His creatures;
for the closing of the Great Hallel is
(תְּהִלִּים קלו, כה) נֹתֵן לֶחֶם לְכָל בָּשָׂר וְגוֹ׳
(Tehillim 136:25) "Who gives bread to all flesh, etc.,"
"Give thanks to the God of heaven,
for from this comes thanksgiving to the God of heaven,
Who sits in the heights of the world
through the power of the Torah;
that is, those who toil in Torah
that their sustenance is from a higher place;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן קוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה
whereas before the giving of the Torah
He had to sustain them in His kindness, may He be blessed.
וְהִנֵּה זֶהוּ נֶגֶד מִדַּת חֶסֶד לְאַבְרָהָם
And this corresponds to the attribute of "Chessed to Avraham,"
And the utterance "Let the earth sprout"
was also on the third day
of the six days of Creation,
which corresponds to the aspect of "Truth to Yaakov,"
in whom the Chessed was confirmed
and through him Avraham's attribute of Chessed was clarified,
for Avraham too is called Yisrael
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סג, ג)
"Remember the Shabbos day to sanctify it,"
and Chazal, of blessed memory, expounded
כִּי עִיקַּר הַשְׁרָאַת הַקְּדוּשָּׁה שֶׁל שַׁבָּת
For the main resting of the holiness of Shabbos
which is from the power of the Torah:
for the Torah was given to Yisrael on Shabbos
And that is, one who partakes of a meal
at which talmidei chachamim are reclining
is as though he enjoyed the radiance of the Shechinah
"Are you more precious to us than it?"
is a semblance of the World to Come,
with their crowns on their heads
and enjoy the radiance of the Shechinah.
And this corresponds to the utterance "Let the earth sprout":
when is the holy land made to flourish?
And also according to the Zohar,
the third utterance is "Let the waters gather, etc.,"
which is the revealing of the land;
a share in the World to Come,
'And your people, etc., will inherit the land.'"
And Binah is the World to Come,
and about it the Zohar said "the holy land."
For at the time of Creation
in the holiness of Eretz Yisrael;
that is, on the Shabbos day:
through the holiness of the Shabbos meal.
And as is written in the holy Zohar
every day from the supernal spirit
it delights in the delight of the body,
with a crown above and below."
For the matter of a crown
is from the aspect of the Kesser
which is beyond the grasp of the mind,
in the vessel of the mind;
and it is the aspect of Ayin,
אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיהוּ לָא חָזֵי
in matters in which you are foolish.
And this comes through the additional soul,
from the aspect of Atika Kadisha,
who comes to dine with her;
the land brings forth blessings to the world.
of which it says "and He blessed";
and as it says at the completion of the work of the Mishkan
and it says in the holy Zohar,
"And with what blessing did he bless them?
on the work of your hands";
and so too this "and He blessed" of the seventh day.
And as they said in Tanchuma
"At the creation of the world it is written 'and He blessed,'
and at the Mishkan it is written 'and he blessed,'" etc.
that it should be the source of blessings,

p: with the first utterance, "Let there be light,"
I will make him a helpmate opposite him."
that according to the Gemara's count,
corresponding to the attribute of Kesser,
which is the cessation of grasp,
it is counted as the first utterance,
except that which emerges from within darkness,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ב קפד, א)
as is written (in the holy Zohar II 184a),
even though there is not written
which is the beginning of the revelation
the aspect of something from nothing.
אָמְנָם עַל פִּי הַזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ כָּאן
However, according to the holy Zohar here,
it is because this light too
was hidden away for the tzaddikim for the time to come,
And the second utterance, of separation,
and separation between water and water
for there is the heart of the wise and of the fool,
is "I will make him a helpmate opposite him,"
and it too is included among
that this is the matter of the two opinions
For according to the one who says a face,
that they were created at once two-faced,
in the utterance "I will make him a helpmate,"
then this is not counted as an utterance
and this follows the Gemara's count.
But according to the holy Zohar's count,
like the one who says a tail,
Now according to the Gemara's order,
that Bereishis is also an utterance,
and let the dry land appear,"
which corresponds to the attribute of Chessed,
for from it begins the world of building,
"For I said, the world will be built with kindness";
וְהוּא מִדָּתוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and it is the attribute of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
"These are the products of heaven and earth
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק א קנד, ב)
as is written (in the holy Zohar I 154b).
And this utterance was on the third day,
on which we say the song of the day,
because He revealed the land with His wisdom
and prepared the world for His congregation,
"Let the waters gather into one place."
the root of kindnesses and longings,
of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
all of whose longing and love
"And you shall love Hashem your God."
However, from this there branched out in the world
the land was revealed with His wisdom,
only for His Name, may He be blessed,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הֵכִין תֵּבֵל לַעֲדָתוֹ
and through this He prepared the world for His congregation,
which is the completion of the purpose of Creation.
It turns out that it corresponds exactly
"Remember the Shabbos day to sanctify it,"
by the power of the holiness of Shabbos,
which is the completion of the purpose of Creation,
through the revelation of the illumination of wisdom

p: that the difference in the order of counting
that throughout the account of Creation
and of the actual making it says
(בְּרֵאשִׁית ב, ד) בְּיוֹם עֲשׂוֹת ה׳ אֱלֹקִים
for at first it arose in thought
to create the world with the attribute of judgment,
and He saw that the world could not endure,
so He joined it with the attribute of mercy.
And certainly regarding Him, may He be blessed,
one may not ascribe, chas v'shalom,
is a very lofty mode of governance,
and there is no grasping it
רַק עַל יְדֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
(אִיּוֹב כח, י) וְכָל יְקָר רָאֲתָה עֵינוֹ
(Iyov 28:10) "And his eye saw every precious thing":
this is Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues;
"and all of them, the anonymous teachings,
the governance is with the attribute of judgment,
that with tzaddikim He is exacting
And this is the root of the Talmud Bavli,
that HaKadosh Baruch Hu illuminates their eyes
with the light hidden away for the tzaddikim
And about this it says in the holy Zohar:
know how to conceal matters within them.
the entire Oral Torah in concealment,
such as one who exchanges a cow for a donkey,
and specifically in this are hidden
all the secrets of His governance, may He be blessed.
And as we heard regarding this
זֵכֶר צַדִּיקִים וּקְדוֹשִׁים לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
may the memory of the righteous and holy be a blessing for the life of the World to Come:
that in the future it will be revealed
that there is no movement in this world,
and in all of them there is a holy governance,
And this is the whole matter of the essential halachos
and they are living and enduring forever;
"one who makes a claim after the action of beis din
But in the way of learning of the holy Zohar,
are revealed and explicit to the eye,
are the words of the living God,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ הַתּוֹסָפוֹת (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כז, א)
between Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Eliezer
whether the world was created in Nisan
that these and those are the words of the living God,
for in Tishrei it arose in thought,
which is governance with the attribute of judgment,
and in Nisan it was actually created,
which is governance with the attribute of mercy.
And in this way one can understand
in which the first utterance begins with Bereishis:
even though the pasuk could not
describe it with the term "and He said,"
because it only arose in thought,
in the aspect of "He made darkness His concealment,"
comes the revelation of the light
except that which emerges from within darkness,
(as was explained in Parshas Shemos, maamar 1),
and this is what is hidden away for the tzaddikim
only those in which "and He said" is stated
before "And the heavens were completed, etc.";
which is not so of the utterance
"And He said, etc., I will make him a helpmate,"
which is mentioned regarding the actual making,
בְּיוֹם עֲשׂוֹת ה׳ אֱלֹקִים אֶרֶץ וְגוֹ׳
"on the day Hashem Elokim made earth, etc."
with the first utterance at "Let there be light,"
is also counted among the ten utterances.
this depends on the dispute (in Eruvin 18a)
and these and those are the words of the living God,
as it says there in the Gemara,
that at first it arose in thought
and in the end one was created.
It turns out that according to the Talmud Bavli
the creation of male and female
in the thought of "Let us make man,"
וְלָכֵן לֹא נֶחְשָׁב אֶעֱשֶׂה לּוֹ עֵזֶר
and therefore "I will make him a helpmate" is not counted
but according to the way of the holy Zohar,
which begins from the actual revelation,
in which only one was created,
the utterance "I will make him a helpmate"
on the pasuk "Ten, ten per ladle,"
because it was difficult for it:
that the doubling of the word "ten"
alludes to what was said above:
which are all the matters of the entire world,
are on a single scale in holiness
which are the totality of the Torah.
For the matters of the world too
and this comes through the ketores.
